verdicts.reviewer_notes: Fifth review. Its purpose was to check key obligations 3 and 6 against statute text, because they were last edited from secondary summaries. SOURCE USED: every leginfo.legislature.ca.gov URL returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-06. That covered billTextClient, billNavClient, billPdf for the chaptered version, the codes_displaySection pages for BPC 22757.13 and 22757.15, and Cal. Const. art. IV sec. 8. downloads.leginfo returned 404, and legiscan returned 403. I verified against the Legislative Counsel Bureau's authenticated chaptered PDF of SB 53, Chapter 138. The PDF carries the 'State of California Authenticated Electronic Legal Material' seal and a digital signature block, so the document is the issuing body's own official text. The copy I fetched is hosted by Sidley Austin (https://www.sidley.com/-/media/resource-pages/ai-monitor/laws-and-regulations/cal-sb53-artificial-intelligence-models--large-developers.pdf). It is not on a .ca.gov host, and I did not validate the signature cryptographically. I read all 16 pages in full. OBLIGATION 3: verified verbatim. BPC 22757.13(c)(1) says 'Subject to paragraph (2), a frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident.' 22757.13(c)(2) says 'If a frontier developer discovers that a critical safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction, that is appropriate based on the nature of that incident and as required by law.' The candidate wording matches: 15 days to OES from discovery, and 24 hours to an appropriate authority, not OES, for imminent risk of death or serious physical injury. OBLIGATION 6: verified verbatim. 22757.15(a) says 'A large frontier developer that fails to publish or transmit a compliant document required to be published or transmitted under this chapter, makes a statement in violation of subdivision (e) of Section 22757.12, fails to report an incident as required by Section 22757.13, or fails to comply with its own frontier AI framework shall be subject to a civil penalty in an amount dependent upon the severity of the violation that does not exceed one million dollars ($1,000,000) per violation.' 22757.15(b) says 'A civil penalty described in this section shall be recovered in a civil action brought only by the Attorney General.' The candidate correctly limits the penalty to large frontier developers, and its 'e.g.' list correctly lists only a subset of the four triggers. One web-search summary paraphrased 22757.15(a) as 'a frontier developer'. The authenticated text says 'A large frontier developer', so that paraphrase is wrong and the candidate is right. OTHER CLAIMS, checked against the same text: 10^26 integer or floating-point operations (22757.11(i)(1)). Large frontier developer means more than $500,000,000 in annual gross revenues together with affiliates in the preceding calendar year (22757.11(j)). The candidate omits 'with affiliates', which is acceptable. Framework duties, annual review and the 30-day publication of material modifications are in 22757.12(a) and (b). The transparency report applies to all frontier developers, before or concurrently with deployment (22757.12(c)(1)). Internal-use summaries go to OES 'every three months or pursuant to another reasonable schedule' (22757.12(d)). The anti-retaliation duty applies to 'A frontier developer' (Labor Code 1107.1(a)), and the anonymous internal process applies to 'A large frontier developer' (1107.1(e)(1)). CalCompute is operative 'only upon an appropriation in a budget act, or other measure' (Gov. Code 11546.8(k)). DATES AND STATUS: the PDF header reads 'Approved by Governor September 29, 2025. Filed with Secretary of State September 29, 2025', Chapter 138. The Governor's 2025-09-29 press release (gov.ca.gov) is consistent. The chaptered text has no urgency clause and no delayed operative date for Chapter 25.1. Art. IV sec. 8(c)(1) says a regular-session statute takes effect 'January 1 next following a 90-day period from the date of enactment'. leginfo blocked that page, so I confirmed the wording via a search result quoting it (Wikisource and other copies, not primary). 29 Sep 2025 plus 90 days is 28 Dec 2025, so the statute took effect 1 Jan 2026, and the in_force timeline entry is correct. On amendments: the Governor's 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-30 bill-signing releases list no bill that amends SB 53. A web search found no injunction or federal preemption of SB 53 as of the latest reports. This was a search, not exhaustive, so status 'in_force' rests on no contrary evidence found. TIER: both timeline URLs are leginfo, which is primary (state legislature) and the correct citation, although they are currently blocked to automated fetch. DUPLICATE: a grep of content/ outside runs/ for SB 53, 'Frontier Artificial Intelligence' and 22757 found nothing. The only other frontier-model entry in the file is NY RAISE, a different jurisdiction. TONE: neutral. NON-BLOCKING NOTE: the summary's 'Enforced by the Attorney General' is accurate for the 22757.15 civil penalty. Two points are not captured. The whistleblower provisions are also enforceable by covered employees in civil actions (Labor Code 1107.1(f) and (h)). The 22757.15 penalty does not reach frontier developers that are not large. A future edit could add both points. Neither makes the current text false.
